taxonomic_note: Legacy/source concept Mimosa aculeaticarpa var. biuncifera normalized to Mimosa biuncifera.
look_here_first: Woody catclaw mimosa with many pairs of pinnae, strongly hooked infrastipular prickles, pale pink to whitish flower heads, and pods constricted between seeds.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Legacy source normalized to current Kew-accepted Mimosa biuncifera. UT Plant Resources Center treats the western white catclaw concept separately from the native NW Hays M. texana populations.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Fabaceae/Mimosa: bipinnate leaves, pulvini that can drive touch-sensitive movement in several species, globose heads of many tiny flowers, and segmented/prickly legumes. Habit, prickle placement, pinna count, and pod structure are especially useful.
best_field_traits: 1–2 strongly recurved prickles near leaf nodes
pale pink to whitish globose heads
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with M. texana, it usually has more pinnae and leaflet pairs, prickles arising near the stipules, and more strongly constricted pods.
